L195: ## NAME
L196: 
L197: git-hash-object - Compute object ID and optionally create an object from a file
L198: 
L199: ## SYNOPSIS
L200: 
L201:     git hash-object [-t <type>] [-w] [--path=<file> | --no-filters]
L202:     		[--stdin [--literally]] [--] <file>…​
L203:     git hash-object [-t <type>] [-w] --stdin-paths [--no-filters]
L204: ## DESCRIPTION
L205: 
L206: Computes the object ID value for an object with specified type with the contents of the named file (which can be outside of the work tree), and optionally writes the resulting object into the object database. Reports its object ID to its standard output. When <type> is not specified, it defaults to "blob".
L207: ## OPTIONS
L208: 
L209: -t <type>
L210: 
L211: 
L212: Specify the type of object to be created (default: "blob"). Possible values are `commit`, `tree`, `blob`, and `tag`.
L213: 
L214: -w
L215: 
L216: 
L217: Actually write the object into the object database.
L218: 
L219: --stdin
L220: 
L221: 
L222: Read the object from standard input instead of from a file.
L223: 
L224: --stdin-paths
L225: 
L226: 
L227: Read file names from the standard input, one per line, instead of from the command-line.
L228: 
L229: --path
L230: Hash object as if it were located at the given path. The location of the file does not directly influence the hash value, but the path is used to determine which Git filters should be applied to the object before it can be placed in the object database. As a result of applying filters, the actual blob put into the object database may differ from the given file. This option is mainly useful for hashing temporary files located outside of the working directory or files read from stdin.
L231: 
L232: --no-filters
L233: Hash the contents as is, ignoring any input filter that would have been chosen by the attributes mechanism, including the end-of-line conversion. If the file is read from standard input then this is always implied, unless the `--path` option is given.
L234: 
L235: --literally
L236: Allow `--stdin` to hash any garbage into a loose object which might not otherwise pass standard object parsing or git-fsck checks. Useful for stress-testing Git itself or reproducing characteristics of corrupt or bogus objects encountered in the wild.

L225: 
L226: `git --version`
L227: ## NAME
L228: 
L229: git-update-index - Register file contents in the working tree to the index
L230: ## SYNOPSIS
L231: 
L232:     git update-index
L233:     	     [--add] [--remove | --force-remove] [--replace]
L234:     	     [--refresh] [-q] [--unmerged] [--ignore-missing]
L235:     	     [(--cacheinfo <mode>,<object>,<file>)…​]
L236:     	     [--chmod=(+|-)x]
L237:     	     [--[no-]assume-unchanged]
L238:     	     [--[no-]skip-worktree]
L239:     	     [--[no-]ignore-skip-worktree-entries]
L240:     	     [--[no-]fsmonitor-valid]
L241:     	     [--ignore-submodules]
L242:     	     [--[no-]split-index]
L243:     	     [--[no-|test-|force-]untracked-cache]
L244:     	     [--[no-]fsmonitor]
L245:     	     [--really-refresh] [--unresolve] [--again | -g]
L246:     	     [--info-only] [--index-info]
L247:     	     [-z] [--stdin] [--index-version <n>]
L248:     	     [--show-index-version]
L249:     	     [--verbose]
L250:     	     [--] [<file>…​]
L251: ## DESCRIPTION
L252: 
L253: Modifies the index. Each file mentioned is updated into the index and any unmerged or needs updating state is cleared.
L254: 
L255: See also cite48†git-add[1] for a more user-friendly way to do some of the most common operations on the index.
L256: 
L257: The way git update-index handles files it is told about can be modified using the various options:
L258: ## OPTIONS
L259: 
L260: --add
L261: 
L262: 
L263: If a specified file isn’t in the index already then it’s added. Default behaviour is to ignore new files.
L264: 
L265: --remove
L266: 
L267: 
L268: If a specified file is in the index but is missing then it’s removed. Default behavior is to ignore removed files.
L269: 
L270: --refresh
L271: 
L272: 
L273: Looks at the current index and checks to see if merges or updates are needed by checking stat() information.
L274: 
L275: -q
L276: Quiet. If --refresh finds that the index needs an update, the default behavior is to error out. This option makes git update-index continue anyway.
L277: 
L278: --ignore-submodules
L279: 
L280: 
L281: Do not try to update submodules. This option is only respected when passed before --refresh.
L282: 
L283: --unmerged
L284: 
L285: 
L286: If --refresh finds unmerged changes in the index, the default behavior is to error out. This option makes git update-index continue anyway.
L287: 
L288: --ignore-missing
L289: 
L290: 
L291: Ignores missing files during a --refresh
L292: --cacheinfo <mode>,<object>,<path>
L293: --cacheinfo <mode> <object> <path>
L294: 
L295: 
L296: Directly insert the specified info into the index. For backward compatibility, you can also give these three arguments as three separate parameters, but new users are encouraged to use a single-parameter form.
L297: 
L298: --index-info
L299: 
L300: 
L301: Read index information from stdin.
L302: 
L303: --chmod=(+|-)x
L304: 
L305: 
L306: Set the execute permissions on the updated files.
L307: 
L308: --assume-unchanged
L309: --no-assume-unchanged
L310: When this flag is specified, the object names recorded for the paths are not updated. Instead, this option sets/unsets the "assume unchanged" bit for the paths. When the "assume unchanged" bit is on, the user promises not to change the file and allows Git to assume that the working tree file matches what is recorded in the index. If you want to change the working tree file, you need to unset the bit to tell Git.
L311: This is sometimes helpful when working with a big project on a filesystem that has a very slow lstat(2) system call (e.g. cifs).
L312: Git will fail (gracefully) in case it needs to modify this file in the index e.g. when merging in a commit; thus, in case the assumed-untracked file is changed upstream, you will need to handle the situation manually.
L313: 
L314: --really-refresh
L315: 
L316: 
L317: Like `--refresh`, but checks stat information unconditionally, without regard to the "assume unchanged" setting.
L318: 
L319: --skip-worktree
L320: --no-skip-worktree
L321: When one of these flags is specified, the object names recorded for the paths are not updated. Instead, these options set and unset the "skip-worktree" bit for the paths. See section "Skip-worktree bit" below for more information.
L322: 
L323: --ignore-skip-worktree-entries
L324: --no-ignore-skip-worktree-entries
L325: 
L326: 
L327: Do not remove skip-worktree (AKA "index-only") entries even when the `--remove` option was specified.
L328: 
L329: --fsmonitor-valid
L330: --no-fsmonitor-valid
L331: When one of these flags is specified, the object names recorded for the paths are not updated. Instead, these options set and unset the "fsmonitor valid" bit for the paths. See section "File System Monitor" below for more information.
L332: 
L333: -g
L334: --again
L335: 
L336: 
L337: Runs git update-index itself on the paths whose index entries are different from those of the `HEAD` commit.
L338: 
L339: --unresolve
L340: 
L341: 
L342: Restores the unmerged or needs updating state of a file during a merge if it was cleared by accident.
L343: 
L344: --info-only
L345: Do not create objects in the object database for all <file> arguments that follow this flag; just insert their object IDs into the index.
L346: 
L347: --force-remove
L348: 
L349: 
L350: Remove the file from the index even when the working directory still has such a file. (Implies --remove.)
L351: 
L352: --replace
L353: By default, when a file `path` exists in the index, git update-index refuses an attempt to add `path/file`. Similarly if a file `path/file` exists, a file `path` cannot be added. With --replace flag, existing entries that conflict with the entry being added are automatically removed with warning messages.
L354: 
L355: --stdin
L356: 
L357: 
L358: Instead of taking a list of paths from the command line, read a list of paths from the standard input. Paths are separated by LF (i.e. one path per line) by default.
L359: 
L360: --verbose
L361: Report what is being added and removed from the index.
L362: 
L363: --index-version <n>
L364: 
L365: 
L366: Write the resulting index out in the named on-disk format version. Supported versions are 2, 3, and 4. The current default version is 2 or 3, depending on whether extra features are used, such as `git` `add` `-N`. With `--verbose`, also report the version the index file uses before and after this command.
L367: Version 4 performs a simple pathname compression that reduces index size by 30%-50% on large repositories, which results in faster load time. Git supports it since version 1.8.0, released in October 2012, and support for it was added to libgit2 in 2016 and to JGit in 2020. Older versions of this manual page called it "relatively young", but it should be considered mature technology these days.
L368: 
L369: --show-index-version
L370: Report the index format version used by the on-disk index file. See `--index-version` above.
L371: 
L372: -z
L373: 
L374: 
L375: Only meaningful with `--stdin` or `--index-info`; paths are separated with NUL character instead of LF.
L376: 
L377: --split-index
L378: --no-split-index
L379: 
L380: 
L381: Enable or disable split index mode. If split-index mode is already enabled and `--split-index` is given again, all changes in $GIT_DIR/index are pushed back to the shared index file.
L382: These options take effect whatever the value of the `core.splitIndex` configuration variable (see cite42†git-config[1] ). But a warning is emitted when the change goes against the configured value, as the configured value will take effect next time the index is read and this will remove the intended effect of the option.
L383: 
L384: --untracked-cache
L385: --no-untracked-cache
L386: 
L387: 
L388: Enable or disable untracked cache feature. Please use `--test-untracked-cache` before enabling it.
L389: These options take effect whatever the value of the `core.untrackedCache` configuration variable (see cite42†git-config[1] ). But a warning is emitted when the change goes against the configured value, as the configured value will take effect next time the index is read and this will remove the intended effect of the option.
L390: 
L391: --test-untracked-cache
L392: Only perform tests on the working directory to make sure untracked cache can be used. You have to manually enable untracked cache using `--untracked-cache` or `--force-untracked-cache` or the `core.untrackedCache` configuration variable afterwards if you really want to use it. If a test fails the exit code is 1 and a message explains what is not working as needed, otherwise the exit code is 0 and OK is printed.
